subject: Clarify: token rounding, long-context accounting, and pilot packaging
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@brightarc.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-10T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Billing mechanics for long-context usage and partial tokens

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for the demo last week — the latency and cost profile looked promising for our enterprise search+assistant use case. Before we push a pilot, procurement asked for a short write-up on how Redwood will meter our usage. A few specific questions they want documented: 

- How do you round partial tokens? If our requests average 12.3 tokens per call, are those rounded per-call or aggregated?
- For long-context requests (we plan to send up to 50k tokens occasionally), is context length charged as the full context every call or do you apply any prefix/KV caching credits?
- Is there a minimum charge per request or a per-call floor?
- If we commit to a 6-month pilot, what packaging or discount flexibility exists for smoothing/aggregation?

I attached a small sample of our projected daily sample (usage-sample.csv) so you can see the distribution.

Can you summarize these mechanics in a short note we can share with procurement?

Best,
Elena
Procurement & Ops
BrightArc

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@brightarc.com>
Date: 2028-06-11T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Billing mechanics for long-context usage and partial tokens

Elena — thanks for the sample and the clear questions. High level summary below, plus a couple of options for pilots. Happy to turn this into a one-page PDF for procurement.

Quick answers (short):
- Rounding: we meter at token granularity but apply a configurable aggregation window for billing. Default hosted behavior is per-call rounding up to 1 token (i.e., ceil per-call). For pilots we can enable daily aggregation which sums tokens across a 24h window and then applies rounding at the window level (less rounding overhead for many small calls).
- Long-context: we charge for the actual tokens passed to the model. For repeated inference where identical prefixes are present, our runtime can apply KV/prefix caching which reduces billed context for warm requests — we measure and report KV reuse percentage on the Console. Cache savings are accounted as reductions to billed tokens in usage exports.
- Minimums: there is a per-request minimum for some legacy SKUs (10 tokens floor). Hosted modern SKUs default to no per-request floor when aggregation is enabled; otherwise we recommend a small floor (10 tokens) to avoid microburst abuse.
- Pilot packaging: we typically offer daily aggregation + a committed spend discount. For example: enable daily aggregation, round total daily tokens to nearest 10 tokens (vs per-call ceil), and apply a temporary commit credit (see options below).

Illustrative math using your sample: assume 1,000 calls/day averaging 12.3 tokens.
- Per-call ceil: 1,000 * ceil(12.3) = 1,000 * 13 = 13,000 billed tokens
- Daily aggregation, round to nearest 10: sum = 12,300 -> round(12,300 / 10) * 10 = 12,300 (no change here) but microcalls that average small values benefit more. In a mixed distribution daily aggregation typically reduces rounding overhead by ~2-6% for customer profiles like yours.

Pilot options I recommend: 
A) Standard pilot (no change): per-call ceil, no discount.
B) Aggregation pilot: enable daily aggregation, rounding to nearest 10 tokens, include telemetry on KV reuse; we offer a 7% usage credit for first 90 days.
C) Committed pilot: 3-month min spend commit -> 10% committed discount + daily aggregation.

I attached a draft SOW (SOW_v2.pdf) and a pricing sheet. If you want, I can loop in Vanessa (sales) and Marissa (finance) to confirm discounts and finalize SOW language.

Cheers,
Mateo
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Looping you both in — good proposal from Mateo. BrightArc is strategic and the pilot looks likely to expand if latency/cost match expectations.

Proposal (sales):
- Approve option B (Aggregation pilot) as default negotiated pilot.
- Offer a one-time onboarding credit equal to 10% of projected first-month usage to help them test longer contexts.
- Add a clause in SOW: for the duration of the pilot we will enable daily aggregation and round to the nearest 10 tokens. Engineering will enable KV prefix caching telemetry so BrightArc can see reuse rates.

Ask Marissa: can finance approve the 10% onboarding credit as a contra-revenue promotion? If not, propose counter.

Thanks — Vanessa
Director, Sales

Date: 2028-06-13T11:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Billing mechanics for long-context usage and partial tokens

Vanessa, Mateo — thanks for the context and the projected numbers. Finance notes:

- We can approve a promotional credit but prefer it as a time-limited usage credit (applied on invoice) rather than a permanent price change.
- 10% is higher than our standard pilot concession for new accounts; I recommend 7% for the first 90 days (usage credit). We can do 10% only if the account signs a 6-month committed spend (minimum $40k).
- Operationally, daily aggregation + rounding to nearest 10 tokens is fine — engineering should confirm the export flags so procurement sees the exact billed tokens vs raw tokens. Attach redlined SOW (SOW_v2.pdf) and a pricing-sheet.xlsx with the adjusted credit rows.

I'll approve the 7% credit for a 90-day pilot and will process the contra-credit in our billing system if the SOW hits 3-way signoff.

Marissa Cole
Manager, Revenue Ops & Billing

Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-15T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Billing mechanics for long-context usage and partial tokens — pilot terms

Elena / Josh — following up with final pilot terms per internal approvals. Summary below and attached SOW_v3_for_signature.pdf.

Agreed pilot terms: 
- Aggregation behavior: enable daily aggregation (24h window) for all pilot usage. Billable tokens = sum(raw tokens) per day, rounded to the nearest 10 tokens.
- KV/prefix caching: enabled when workload patterns allow; KV reuse will be surfaced on the Console export and reflected as billed reductions.
- Rounding/minimums: no per-call floor during pilot because daily aggregation is enabled. Post-pilot standard per-call ceil may apply unless a committed SKU is adopted.
- Promotional credit: 7% usage credit applied to usage invoices for first 90 days of pilot. If BrightArc signs a 6-month committed agreement with $40k minimum spend, we will increase the credit to 10% and provide an additional onboarding services waiver.
- Documentation & signatures: SOW_v3_for_signature.pdf attached and DocuSign link below.

Attachments included: SOW_v3_for_signature.pdf (redlines applied), pricing-sheet.xlsx (final), usage-sample.csv (provided by BrightArc).

Next steps:
1) Elena — confirm you have procurement approval for the 7% 90-day credit and daily aggregation.
2) If yes, I will send DocuSign for SOW_v3 (link: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/BRIGHTARC-SOW-V3).

Thanks — looking forward to getting the pilot started.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
